title: Inelastic Collision of Two Particles — Direction of Combined Particle

question.statement: Two particles $A$ and $B$ of equal mass $M$ are moving with the same speed $v$ as shown in the figure. They collide completely inelastically and move as a single particle $C$. The angle $\theta$ that the path of $C$ makes with the $X$-axis is given by:

solution_methods.steps: By integrating external impulse over the duration of the impact, total momentum change equals zero in the horizontal plane, yielding the exact center-of-mass displacement directly without integrating coordinates.

figure_refs.caption: Two particles A and B moving at angles 30° and 45° to the X-axis, colliding to form particle C at angle theta
figure_refs.alt_text: A coordinate system with X and Y axes. Particle A moves upward and to the right at 30 degrees to the positive X-axis. Particle B moves downward and to the left at 45 degrees below the negative X-axis. Particle C moves upward to the right at angle theta to the positive X-axis after the collision.
